questions.passage: Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories. A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average. One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things. When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others. By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of "confirmation bias." That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn't support them. During election season, for example, , while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.
options: ① political advertisements are banned to reduce misinformation
② the public demands stronger legal actions against fake news creators
③ people become more careful about checking the reliability of news sources
④ individuals tend to support all candidates equally regardless of media content
⑤ voters are likely to accept positive news about their preferred candidates without doubt

questions.passage: With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don't just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don't read the news at face value. Exercise skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don't forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news!
options: ① media diversity
② critical thinking
③ political neutrality

questions.passage: Fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of "confirmation bias." That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn't support them. During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.
options: ① Preventing false information from spreading should be a duty of news outlets.
② During election season, voters tend to make rational decisions based on solid evidence.
③ Critical thinking is unnecessary when the information seems to match people's preferences.
④ Fake news spreads because people uncritically accept information that supports their beliefs.
⑤ Relying on information based on personal experience is the most effective way to avoid fake news.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don't just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don't read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don't forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news!
options: ① technology used to spread fake news
② complications of regulating online information
③ ways to avoid being misled by fake news on the Internet
④ problems caused by the overload of information on the Internet
⑤ new functions of online media that help readers find reliable sources

questions.passage: Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories. A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average. One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things. When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others. By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of "confirmation bias." That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn't support them. During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.
options: ① A study showed that fake news spreads online at the same speed as true news.
② People tend to avoid surprising or provocative news on social media.
③ Fake news spreads partly because people like to be the first to share unusual information. M(박준언) 1단원
④ Most people critically examine new information before believing it.
⑤ Confirmation bias helps people recognize the flaws in their own beliefs.

questions.passage: With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don't just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don't read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don't forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news!

With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines.

공통영어2 YBM(박

They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don't just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don't read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don't forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news!
options: ① Provocative headlines can mislead readers into clicking without reading carefully.
② Readers are encouraged to examine their own biases while evaluating news.
③ The passage advises readers to avoid reading any news that disagrees with their opinions.
④ It is important to verify the writer's intent and the credibility of the news source.
⑤ Critical thinking helps minimize the damage caused by fake news in the digital world.

questions.passage:
Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories. A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average.

(A) One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things. When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others. (B) Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. (C) By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information. (D) Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of "confirmation bias." That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn't support them.

During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.

ⓐ A village in a dry area created a simple clay refrigerator that does not use electricity. It is made by placing one clay pot inside another and filling the space between with wet sand. Local people can build it with cheap clay, and they do not need outside experts to repair it.

ⓑ In a small rural community, a large steel factory produces advanced solar panels that are shipped overseas. ⓒ Farmers in a mountain region made water pumps from bamboo pipes. The pumps use the natural flow of streams to bring water to their rice fields without fuel or electricity. Villagers set up and repair the pumps themselves, and the materials come directly from the surrounding forest.

ⓓ A city government built an expensive waste treatment plant that uses complex chemical processes. Only a few technicians from abroad can operate the system, and spare parts must be imported at high cost. While the plant is useful, the local residents cannot manage or repair it on their own.

ⓔ In many cities, artificial intelligence is widely used to manage traffic, recommend products, and control home devices. It gives people convenience, but it depends on advanced algorithms and global networks rather than local resources.

News Release Date: August 16, 2024

DEATH VALLEY, Calif.

A Death Valley National Park resort employee was rescued on August 13 after becoming severely dehydrated while hiking Panamint Butte.

The man started hiking at 3 am from Panamint Springs Resort. He crossed Panamint Valley, then climbed Panamint Butte's wast face. He had hiked more than 8  miles and gained 4,600 feet in elevation. He got to the summit around noon. Then it was time to head back.

He consulted a topographic map and decided to descend through a canyon. The man came to a rappel anchor at the top of a dryfall. Not having ropes and technical gear, he climbed back up the mountain and descended the route he had climbed that morning.

He ran out of water around 4:30 pm.

Heat and dehydration caught up with him. He reports that he lost consciousness and slid down a scree slope. After an unknown period of time, he woke up bruised and realized it was time to call for a rescue. He used the SOS function on his Garmin around 6:00 pm.

The National Park Service (NPS) and Inyo County Sheriff's Office got the request for assistance around 7:40 pm. The first agency contacted did not have a helicopter available. The VX-31 "Dust Devils" at Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake took the mission, but were delayed by needing to trouble shoot an alarm on the helicopter. The Navy helicopter rescued the hiker around 11:15 pm.

questions.passage:
Appropriate technology refers to technological solutions that are designed to suitably meet the specific needs of a community. Such technologies typically utilize locally available resources, so they reduce costs and promote local industries. These technologies are environmentally sustainable because they rely on renewable resources. Additionally, their designs are easy to use, which allow local communities to maintain the technologies without specialized training.

The Warka Tower is one good example of appropriate technology. This tower helps with the lack of clean water in many regions. It employs natural processes to deliver 100 liters of clean water daily. It gathers rainwater in a pot at its base. Additionally, the tower captures fog and changes it into water drops that collect on nets, and then the water drops fall into the pot. One of the tower's strengths is that it is simple. A small team can construct it in just one day by using eco-friendly materials like soil, wood, and natural fiber nets. Truly, the Warka Tower demonstrates how appropriate technology can solve local issues in a way that is affordable, effective, and eco-friendly.

questions.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U.S. who founded Home Again in 2016. It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing. He says, "For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated."

John's journey began in 2015. At the age of twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying. He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in. This prompted John to decide to do something for those transitioning out of homelessness. Needing donations to gather essential items to help them, John reached out to his family, friends, and neighbors. As word of his efforts spread, donations began to rush in. So John was able to help more people get settled. He said, "I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a kitchen table could have. Furniture can restore the dignity of a family."
options: ① Temporary Shelters: The Flawed Solution to Homelessness
② From Shelter to Stability: One Boy's Mission to Build Real Homes
③ Ending Homelessness: How Home Again Provides Permanent Housing Solutions
④ Furniture for the Disadvantaged: One Teen's Effort to Bring Comfort and Dignity
⑤ Beyond Charity: A Young Activist Addresses the Emotional Cost of Homelessness

questions.passage: Trisha Prabhu, a young computer scientist from the U.S., is addressing cyberbullying through her innovative initiative, ReThink. This application functions as a virtual keyboard on mobile devices and works across platforms — from Instagram to Twitter — to detect potentially offensive messages before they are posted. When a user types something hurtful, such as “I hate you,” the app intervenes with a prompt like “Hold on! Are you sure you want to post that?” or “Remember, you are what you type!” The initiative began in 2014, when thirteen-year-old Trisha read about a twelve-year-old girl who had been cyberbullied for more than a year, leading to a tragic outcome. Her research shows that 93 percent of adolescents change their minds when receiving ReThink’s alert. By encouraging users to pause and reconsider, the initiative promotes responsible digital citizenship and greater kindness online.

In Korea, nearly anything can be delivered within twenty-four hours. Delivery is not limited to Korea; however, a unique culture has developed around the Korean delivery industry. People in Korea can order whatever they want whenever they want and ⓐhave it delivered wherever they want. Delivery apps rank stores by various standards: review scores, popularity, price, delivery fee, and distance, to name a few. The speedy delivery of purchased items to your house is literally at the tips of your fingers. What is the history behind this culture?

In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary entry after taking the gwageo, a public service entrance exam. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang's diary is the first historical document ⓑindicated Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries.

During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance.

During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul's streets were filled with delivery professionals called "messengers," ⓒworked for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery.

After Korea's liberation from colonial rule, it was divided into two. Then came the Korean War (1950-1953). During this series of upheavals, Korea's delivery system fell apart. It was during the 1960s ⓓthat delivery services grew again thanks to urbanization. As economic development progressed, people flocked to urban areas, where labor became concentrated. This boosted the demand for delivery services. Deliveries of newspapers and milk quickly became popular. During lunchtime, city centers were filled with restaurant workers delivering trays full of food, stacked on top of each other. In the late 1980s and 1990s, caterers delivered homemade lunches in cloth bags to urban offices and returned later to collect empty dishes. The delivery area grew rapidly.

In 1992, taekbae service, an express home delivery service ⓔthrough which a person receives an ordered item in at least a day or two was introduced. On the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now, millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year. It was the development of digital and information technology that enabled the remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation, GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended the range and scale of delivery services while keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery services.

A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if a person orders something today, it should arrive tomorrow. Taekbae is changing ⓕso rapidly that now more and more items are delivered on the same day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose a specific date and time for delivery.

Taekbae services, beginning from foot-powered delivery, have grown by leaps and bounds thanks to advancements in technology. Moreover, the services will likely be developed further due to continuing technological upheavals. Drones and autonomous robots are being used to deliver items by logistics companies in foreign countries. In Korea, companies are testing the possibility of using advanced equipment such as autonomous vehicles, delivery robots, and drones for deliveries. (A)__________________
options: ① The Shift in Korean Delivery: From Personal Reliability to Digital Efficiency
② Taekbae: The Economic Impact of South Korea's Next-Day Express Delivery
③ The Challenges and Future of Autonomous Delivery in Korea
④ Korean Delivery and Logitics Automation Challenges
⑤ A Current Study of Professional Delivery System

Mumbai, India's largest and busiest city, has a unique tradition in which people enjoy home-cooked lunches delivered from their homes. This service is carried out by dedicated people known as dabbawalas.

The delivery process begins early in the morning when lunch boxes are collected by dabbawalas from homes around Mumbai by 9:00 a.m. They are then taken to the nearest train station. Each lunch box is carefully placed on the right train heading in various directions. By 12:30 p.m., the lunches have reached their destinations in Mumbai, where they are distributed to offices. The empty lunch boxes are gathered by 5:00 p.m and returned to their original homes by following the same route in reverse. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang's diary is the first historical document indicating Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries. During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance. During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul's streets were filled with delivery professionals called "messengers," most working for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery.

questions.passage:
(A)

In 1930s Seoul, a group of sharply dressed men on bicycles became a familiar sight. They were “messengers” working for Yongdalsa, a professional delivery company. They became known for their speed and remarkable reliability. Once contacted, a messenger would promptly pick up and deliver items, using bicycles to navigate the city’s narrow streets. Mistakes were almost unheard of. Even large sums of cash or important documents were delivered without error — often without customers checking the contents.

One 1933 case stands out: a bank sent a bundle of 10,000 won (worth a luxury apartment at the time) via Yongdalsa. The messenger delivered it accurately, without any seals or supervisions. A foreign journalist reportedly was amazed at the trust Koreans placed in this system, saying it was only possible because of a strong culture of mutual trust. This unique system laid the groundwork for Korea’s modern delivery services.

* supervision: 감독, 관리

(B)

In July 2025, a shocking incident happened in Korea when a delivery driver was caught stealing a package he had just delivered. After dropping off the parcel at the customer’s door, the driver took the standard proof-of-delivery photo and left on his motorcycle. However, minutes later, he returned, picked up the package, and walked away. The customer, puzzled by the missing package despite the delivery confirmation, reviewed security footage and discovered the theft. The video clearly showed the same driver taking the item after documenting its delivery. Police launched an investigation, and the driver was soon identified and arrested. During questioning, he claimed financial hardship had driven him to commit the theft. The incident sparked public outrage, especially because the thief was the very person trusted to deliver the item.
questions.answer: The 1933 case showed a delivery culture based on strong mutual trust, whereas the 2025 case revealed a serious breakdown of that trust.

questions.passage: In the forty-fourth year of King Yeongjo, seventh month (1768), the day after sitting for the state examination, I lodged with my companions at a guesthouse in Hanyang. The heat was fierce, and by noon my craving for naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) grew urgent. I summoned a runner and had him place an order at a nearby noodle house. I asked that beef brisket be laid atop my bowl, while my companions requested boiled egg for theirs. Before long the bowls arrived. The chill of the crock touched my hands, and at the first sip the cold broth seemed to sink straight into my chest, letting me forget the midsummer heat for a moment. The delivery man left the bowls and departed; we paid the price when he later returned to retrieve the dishes. Across the corridor, other lodgers, too, sent for naengmyeon from the same shop, so that I came to see how common it has become, in these days, to call food to one’s lodging. Having emptied our bowls, we discussed our next steps and steadied ourselves to face the heat again.

questions.passage: In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary entry after taking the gwageo, a public service entrance exam. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang’s diary is the first historical document indicating Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries. During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance. During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul’s streets were filled with delivery professionals called “messengers,” most working for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery.

On the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now, millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year. It was the development of digital and information technology that enabled the remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation, GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended the range and scale of delivery services while keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery services. A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if a person orders something today, it should arrive tomorrow. Taekbae is changing so rapidly that now more and more items are delivered on the same day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose a specific date and time for delivery.
options: ① Taekbae service was introduced in 1992, starting with only two deliveries on the first day.
② The rapid growth of taekbae is largely due to advances in digital and information technology, including GPS and automation.
③ The surge in e-commerce demand has been a significant factor driving the expansion of delivery services.
④ Customers typically expect delivery times to be within three to four days after placing an order.
⑤ Customers can now choose specific delivery dates and times, showing increased flexibility in the service.
questions.explain: "익일 배송(next-day delivery)"이 기본 원칙이라고 하였으므로, ④ '고객들은 보통 주문한 후 3~4일 이내에 배송받기를 기대한다'는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. [오답노트] ① 택배 서비스는 1992년에 도입되어 첫날 단 두 건의 배송이 있었다. ② 택배의 급성장은 GPS와 자동화 등 디지털 및 정보기술 발전 덕분이다. ③ 전자상거래 수요 급증이 배송 서비스 확장의 주요 요인이다. ⑤ 고객은 현재 특정 배송 날짜와 시간을 선택할 수 있어 서비스 유연성이 늘었다.

questions.passage: Taekbae services, beginning from foot-powered delivery, have grown by leaps and bounds thanks to advancements in technology. Moreover, the services will likely be developed further due to continuing technological upheavals. Drones and autonomous robots are being used to deliver items by logistics companies in foreign countries. In Korea, companies are testing the possibility of using advanced equipment such as autonomous vehicles, delivery robots, and drones for deliveries. It is fair to say that modern Korean life cannot function as it does without its delivery services. To maintain trust with customers, the Korean delivery industry prioritizes rapid, safe, and affordable transportation. ④ 한국 배달 회사들은 느리고 안전한 운송을 우선시한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: In Korea, nearly anything can be delivered within twenty-four hours. Delivery is not limited to Korea; however, a unique culture has developed around the Korean delivery industry. People in Korea can order whatever they want whenever they want and have it delivered wherever they want. Delivery apps rank stores by various standards: review scores, popularity, price, delivery fee, and distance, to name a few. The speedy delivery of purchased items to your house is literally at the tips of your fingers. What is the history behind this culture? In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary entry after taking the gwageo, a public service entrance exam. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang’s diary is the first historical document indicating Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries. During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance. During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul’s streets were filled with delivery professionals called “messengers,” most working for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery.
options: ① The first document about delivery in Korea was written by Hwang Yun-seok who ordered food before the gwageo, a public service entrance exam.
② The price of jeonin service was fixed regardless of distance and schedule.
③ Only jeonin who often delivered large bundles of cash had to be familiar with the local areas.
④ Messengers in the colonial period were so reliable that even money was delivered by them.
⑤ There are still some people in Korea who have limited access to delivery service through Internet.
questions.explain: ④ 식민지 시대의 '메신저'은 신뢰가 높아서 심지어 현금을 배달하기도 했다는 글의 내용과 일치한다. [오답 해석] 배달에 관한 최초의 문서는 과거 시험 전이 아니라 과거 시험 후의 내용을 기록하고 있으므로 ① '한국 배달에 관한 최초의 문서는 공무원 시험인 과거를 치르기 전에 음식을 주문했던 황윤석에 의해 쓰여졌다'는 일치하지 않는다. 서비스의 가격은 일정과 거리에 따라 결정되었으므로' 거리와 일정과는 관계없이 가격이 고정되었다'는 ②는 일치하지 않는다. 현대식 주소 체계 전에는 메신저들이 지역을 상세하게 알고 있어 야만 했다고 했으므로 ③ '큰 현금을 배달하는 메신저만이 현지 지역에 익숙해야 했다'는 일치하지 않는다. 현대 한국인들은 언제 어디서나 어떤 것이든 배달 서비스 이용이 가능하다고 했으므로 ⑤ '인터넷을 통한 배달 서비스 이용에 제한이 있는 사람들이 여전히 있다'는 일치하지 않는다.

options: ① 조선 시대에는 편지를 배달하는 전업 배달인이 존재했다.
② 전인에게는 지역 정보를 매우 정확히 알고 있는 것이 필수였다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: As the guardian of a talented child, you should be wary of a frequent error many parents make. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. Otherwise, you may end up raising a driven perfectionist, a child who drops out, or something even worse.
options: ① Talented children may become a perfectionist for their own sake.
② Parents should not feel proud of their children’s accomplishments.
③ Showing off a child's achievements helps the child build self-confidence.
④ Constantly bragging about a child has nothing to do with the mental pressure.
⑤ Gifted children may develop unrealistic expectations of themselves due to parental bragging.
questions.explain: 본문은 부모의 자랑이 자녀에게 심리적 압박을 가하고, 비현실적인 기대감을 형성하며, 자녀가 자신의 본래 모습이 아닌 성취 로만 자신을 정의하게 될 위험을 경고하는 내용이므로, ⑤ '재능 있는 자녀는 부모의 자랑으로 인해 비현실적인 기대를 가질 수 있다.가 글의 내용과 일치한다. <오답 해석> ① 재능 있는 자녀는 자기 자신을 위해 완벽주의자가 될 수 있다. ② 부모가 자녀의 성취를 자랑스러워 하면 안된다. ③ 자녀의 성취를 자랑하는 것이 자녀의 자신감을 키우는 데 도움이 된다. ④ 계속해서 자녀를 자랑하는 것은 정신적 압박과 관계 없다.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse. If you have a gifted child, you need to be careful not to fall into this common parent trap.
options: ① brag about your child excessively
② overlook the effort invested by your child
③ pressure your child to study at an advanced level
④ rush to judge what your child will achieve in the future
⑤ demand that your child follow the schedule you think is best
questions.explain: '지나친 자랑은 아이에게 압박과 비현실적 기대를 주어 완벽주의자나 심하면 중도 포기자가 될 위험이 있기 때문에, 아이가 성취가 아닌 있는 그대로의 자신으로 성장하도록 도와야 한다'는 내용의 글이고, 밑줄 친 '함정에 빠지는 것'은 잘못된 행동 자체를 의미하기 때문에, 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은 ① '자녀에 대해 지나치게 자랑하다'이다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of “program” that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us. [from Professional Communication at Work by Joseph L. Chesebro]
options: ① Positive emotions are essential for forming strong social bonds.
② Fear helps us stay alert and react to threats in our environment.
③ Fear can trigger the "fight or flight" response in dangerous situations.
④ Emotions have evolved because they helped humans adapt and survive.
⑤ Emotions have more impact on human behavior than on cognitive processes.
questions.explain: 본문에서는 감정이 인간 행동 뿐만 아니라 주의력과 기억과 같은 인지 과정에도 영향을 미친다고 했지만, 인지 과정과 감정을 비교하여 인간 행동에 어느 것이 더 큰 영향을 미치는지에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ⑤ '감정은 인지 과정보다 인간 행동에 더 큰 영향을 미친다.'는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. [해석] ① 긍정적인 감정은 강한 사회적 유대 형성에 필수적이다. ② 두려움은 우리가 경계심을 유지하고 환경 속의 위협에 반응하도록 돕는다. ③ 두려움은 위험한 상황에서 '싸우거나 도망가려는' 반응을 촉발할 수 있다. ④ 감정은 인간이 적응하고 생존하는 데 도움을 줬기 때문에 진화해왔다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 'AI'에 관한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI’s capacity to translate written and spoken word in real- time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① 노동 시장에서 우위를 점하고 있는 근로자들을 대상으로 한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along — whether it’s the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS — and you start to use it, it’s like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show — whether it’s Wheel of Fortune or The Wire — you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That’s why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along — a new way for humans to communicate — it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it’s about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① in order to understand a medium, we need to study its history
② goggles are designed to protect users from environmental harm
③ new mediums shape their own ways of making us perceive the world
④ as we age, we learn to use more and more mediums for communication
⑤ new mediums are gradually replacing traditional methods for delivering messages

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. “Analogous” traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not “the same” organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. “Homologous” traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being “the same” organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties. [from The Inheritance and Innateness of Grammars by Myrna Gopnik]
options: ① 상사형질은 공통된 기능을 가지고 있기 때문에 동일한 진화 계보에 서 생겨난 것이다.
② 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 기능의 유사성을 비롯하여 모든 부분에서 유사성이 많다.
③ 상동형질은 상사형질과 반대로 동일한 조상으로 내려왔으나, 동일 한 기능이 없어야 한다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 기능은 다르나 동일한 조상에서 내려 온 상동형질의 예시이다.
⑤ 상사성과 상동성을 구별하기 위해, 생물학자들은 가장 자주 사용되 는 특성에 집중한다.

questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ① Parents are likely to feel proud of their gifted children and brag their outstanding performance.
② Parents of gifted children should restrict their bragging about the children to close friends or family.
③ Gifted children might not be able to satisfy unrealistic expectations caused by their parents.
④ Overemphasizing gifted children‘s achievements makes them feel pressured, which can lead to negative consequences.
⑤ Encouraging a child to focus solely on their achievements can help them develop their true self.

questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along — whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS — and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show — whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire — you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along — a new way for humans to communicate — it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① McLuhan asserted that a brand-new medium has concealed a message.
② We learn through TV that not only is the world speedy, but what matters is the outsides and looks.
③ Using a new medium can be compared to using a new type of goggles with their unique colors and lenses.
④ According to McLuhan, the way information is conveyed to us is no more significant than information.
⑤ No matter what TV show we watch, before we accept its message, we view the world as something that looks like television.

questions.passage:
Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight.

"Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse are one of the examples that show "Homologous" traits.
② "Analogous" traits appeared separately in evolution and are in a significant sense not "the same" organ.
③ Whether or not they have the same function, "Homologous" traits share some common structure to demonstrate their being "the same" organ.
④ There is considerable overlap between the wings of birds and the wings of bees besides their use in flight.
⑤ Biologists generally concentrate on the most useless properties of the organs so as to make a distinction between analogy and homology. BOMANL FX PREP 9월8일 종촌고1 B반 답지
